newsitem.title: FRANCE: Envoy said to bring hope for Western Sahara peace.
newsitem.headline: Envoy said to bring hope for Western Sahara peace.

text.p: The Polisario Front, seeking independence of the mainly Moroccan-controlled Western Sahara, hailed U.N. envoy James Baker's trip to North Africa, saying he had restored hope for advancing the stalled peace process.

"The Sahrawi side is convinced of Baker's willingness to forge a peaceful, just and lasting settlement to the Sahrawi question," front leader Mohamed Abdelaziz was quoted on Tuesday by the official Algerian news agency APS as telling a news conference late on Monday.
He was speaking at Polisario's headquarters in the southwestern Algerian town of Tindouf.
Abdelaziz accused Morocco of hampering implementation of a U.N.-sponsored peace plan on the future of the former Spanish colony.
"Morocco is responsible for freezing the peace process because of its attempts to rig the (U.N.-planned) referendum and empty the peace plan of its substance," he said.
Morocco denies the charges, blaming the Polisario for blocking the peace plan.

Baker, a former U.S. Secretary of State, held talks with Abdelaziz in Tindouf on Sunday, the last stop of his tour to the region. It was Baker's first visit since U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan appointed him last month as his personal envoy to the disputed Western Sahara.
Baker also met Morocco's King Hassan, Algerian President Liamine Zeroual and Mauritania's leader Maaouya Sid Ahmed Taya in his four-day visit to the three North African countries.
Abdelaziz said Polisario's decision to set free 85 Moroccan prisoners of war as Baker arrived to Tindouf was a goodwill gesture to help Baker in his diplomatic mission.
The Polisario Front has been holding some 2,000 prisoners of war, some of them for more than 20 years.

A ceasefire, brokered by the United Nations, has been in effect since September 1991. But the U.N. plan calling for referendum, due to be held in 1992, was delayed by continued dispute over who was eligible to vote.
